pairs.why: B's checker squares are bigger and fewer, with simpler pedestal edges, closer to the real table's chunky inlay and soft cracks; A has dense fine checks and stepped base lines.
A keeps the hero's edges few and soft with a dark lens rim like the real lamp; B adds a hard orange band, vent slots and a button, which are extra crisp internal lines.
A has the soft, thick orange rim, soft-edged stripes and a dotted ring like the real clock; B adds a hard floor line and sharper stripe boundaries.
B has denser small edges in the ground, craters and fittings, closer to the busy edge density of the real cards, though the evidence is weak.
A has a dense truss and a clean hero with a dark front rim like the real lamp; B's vents and band add extra hero edges. The difference is slight.
A has no stitched or dotted seam lines, so it's closer to the real chair's smooth, unmarked fabric; B draws stitching along the back panel.
A's hat edges are soft and have no outline; B has a pale cream brim rim that reads as a drawn contour line.
B has crisp rivets, panel seams and port rims on the hero, like the real submarine's rivets and seams; A is smooth with few internal edges.
